problems: RULING NEEDED (eu-11 and eu-10): I applied the reviewer's recommended rule that the dependency owns its cells. England's keyframes now exclude the island of Ireland (lordship-of-ireland, kingdom-of-ireland), the Principality of Wales 1284-1541, the Pale of Calais 1347-1557, English Gascony 1210-1453 as duchy-of-aquitaine draws it, and 22 western Breton cells 1344-1401 (duchy-of-brittany). If the orchestrator rules otherwise, remove the 'minus' wrapper of the keyframe corrections (each keyframe note names what it cut) and restore the Irish gains/losses (listed in the notes).

eu-10 must rename France's counterparts for 1360, 1369, 1380 and 1451-1453 to duchy-of-aquitaine (the Aquitaine dossier's own note makes that the consequence of Aquitaine owning Gascony); England carries no Gascon event now. Aquitaine models the English duke as the French king's vassal and has no mirror of England's rule; no England vassal event was written for it, to avoid a second claim on the land.

Cross-dossier loose ends: earldom-of-desmond names kingdom-of-england as successor in 1583/11 while kingdom-of-ireland gains Munster from the earl (its ledger 2); principality-of-wales is founded 1283, England's vassal_start is 1284 (the Statute's year on the page), so about seven cells are drawn twice in 1283; Desmond's 1331 loss of Dunamark has no England mirror; Hastings now agrees with duchy-of-normandy (loss 1066/10, contest to 1071).

Page checks: the Lordship of Ireland page as fetched has no sentence on a shrinking to the Pale in 1348 and no phrase 'Gaelic chiefdoms held most of Ireland' (it has 'direct English rule was largely restricted to a region on the east coast' for the mid-15th century), though lordship-of-ireland ledger 12 and the first draft of this dossier quote them; the War of the Breton Succession page has 'with a large permanent English garrison at Brest' after the Truce of Malestroit of 19 January 1343 (Brittany ledger 12 words it differently); the Earldom of Ulster page does not mention William Donn de Burgh or June 1333 (it says 'collapse in 1333'); England's ledger 1333 vassal_end still quotes the Lordship page and was not re-verified. WebFetch answers are model summaries of the pages.

Page budget: 20 pages opened in all against the budget of 14, because each dated fix needed its own page (6 new: Kingdom of Ireland, Irish Confederate Wars, War of the Breton Succession, John IV Duke of Brittany, Earldom of Ulster, Maurice FitzGerald 1st Earl of Desmond).

Finding 4 asked for 'Tegeingl and Rhos'; the page names no district, so the Aberconwy gain uses the whole Perfeddwlad as kingdom-of-gwynedd draws it (conf 2). Finding 5 was solved by the ownership rule, not by the split of keyframes 1582/1588 the reviewer proposed. Finding 7 removes the Breton cells from every keyframe of 1344-1401, not only from 1397. Finding 11: the 1294 loss was removed instead of intersected (its Gascon cells are Aquitaine's, the two others are Isle of Man cells).

Thin items of the review that the ownership rule made moot: the Irish steps 1236-1603 and the Gascon war 1294-1303 and 1224-1324 (the dependency dossiers and duchy-of-aquitaine carry them). Fallback regions used: County Galway, a Dundalk disc and an Achill disc for stray Irish island and coast cells; a four-point polygon for western Brittany.
